acceptance_criteria: PostgresAdapter implements the Warehouse port and is selected via warehouseDriver=postgres in the core warehouse factory (the app request path)

tasks.title: Repo-wide quality gate baseline (backend + contract lint/format, FACTORY_* commands)
tasks.objective: Establish the repo-wide quality gate BEFORE new code is written: ESLint + Prettier config and lint/format:check scripts for backend and contract (which have neither), and the four FACTORY_* commands verify.py reads from .envrc. The frontend joins each command when its workspace lands.
acceptance_criteria: backend and contract have ESLint + Prettier config and lint / format:check scripts that run clean; the pre-existing vendored source is excluded from FORMAT checking via a .prettierignore listing those exact files and ledgered as debt (D-0006), while tools/, the config files this task itself adds, and all newly written code are format-checked (executable MJS also linted), the harness-owned .github workflows are excluded because forge upgrade re-vendors them, and .envrc is validated semantically by the guard test rather than by ESLint or Prettier
the .envrc declares FACTORY_STRUCTURAL_CMD, FACTORY_TYPECHECK_CMD, FACTORY_QUALITY_CMD and FACTORY_TEST_CMD under those exact names, verify.py reads all four, and root verify.py is green
FACTORY_QUALITY_CMD covers every workspace that exists at this point (backend + contract) and product CI runs the equivalent aggregate on every push; the frontend is added by frontend-foundation
tasks.reviewer_focus: LAW (cite, do not re-derive): constitution/09-agent-conduct.md §9 — every tool pick must be justified in the plan's Decisions section, not defaulted; §2 — this is a gate, not a style overhaul. PROOF FORM: decision 0009's canonical required-test command is mandatory and a .mjs test does not exempt it — TS_NODE_PROJECT=backend/tsconfig.json ... --require ts-node/register, id = the real leaf test name, path carrying the file. THE MAPPING IS THE CONTRACT, NOT THE NAME: a guard proving only that some npm script exists is worthless — FACTORY_QUALITY_CMD="npm run build" would satisfy it and make verify.py green while linting nothing. The guard must resolve the named scripts to their BODIES and assert the pinned graph (structural = build + both integrity checks; typecheck = both workspaces no-emit; quality = root lint + format:check; tests = backend suite + this guard), and a substring dodge like `echo lint` must fail. ENV OVERRIDE: verify.py PREFERS a pre-set FACTORY_* variable over .envrc, so CI must set none — otherwise the declared gate is bypassed while everything looks green. CI MUST BE EXECUTABLE: verify.py requires an approved plan from the git-local .git/forge/run.json, which a fresh checkout does NOT have, so CI runs the product-owned `npm run verify:ci` aggregate over the same four command bodies — NOT verify.py. Reject any attempt to fabricate factory state in CI or to patch verify.py; vendor integrity forbids modifying frozen harness machinery. CI pins Node 20 + Python 3.11 and runs `npm ci`, or the binaries are absent. This task CREATES .github/workflows/quality.yml; harness-wiring only widens it for the frontend and re-proves it. LINT TOPOLOGY: ONE root flat eslint.config.mjs covers backend/src, contract/src, contract/test AND tools/ — tools/quality-gate.test.mjs belongs to no workspace, so per-workspace configs would leave 'tools is linted' an implementer guess. It is both linted and format-checked. One named root .prettierrc.json GOVERNS both workspaces by being what the scripts point at (Prettier has no workspace extends convention). BLOCKER THIS TASK CLEARS: backend/src/atlasTokens.test.ts reads frontend/app/globals.css at import time and throws, because decision 0006 excluded the vendored Pulse frontend and no frontend/ exists — FACTORY_TEST_CMD cannot be green until it is REMOVED (D-0005; frontend-foundation owns 3F token coverage). Not skipped, not glob-excluded: a temporarily-excluded known failure is the exact false green this gate exists to stop. TYPECHECK: root `typecheck` currently runs build:contract, which EMITS — it satisfies the name without the guarantee; make it invoke both workspaces' own tsc --noEmit and leave emitting to the structural command. SCOPE: the named manifests, configs, one workflow, the guard test, and that one ledgered deletion. No behaviour change to vendored source; no reformat-the-world commit that would bury later diffs and break the 'Pulse @ commit' review model (decision 0008). Reject BOTH a ruleset weakened until it reports nothing AND a broad vendored-source remediation smuggled in under a baseline task — the latter is a stop-and-replan. NEGATIVE CONTROLS (decision 0009), one per tool and distinct: a parse/obvious-error violation fails ESLint but not Prettier; formatting-only drift fails Prettier but not the syntax-only ESLint policy; and all three mapping failures (missing variable, misspelled script, command repointed at a non-linting command) fail the guard. A test that cannot fail proves nothing. NOTE: contract/test is outside the contract tsconfig includes and has no runnable suite — that stays deferred (D-0002); this task lints and formats it, nothing more. FORMAT SCOPE (human decision 2026-09-07, signal S-0007-8b73, deferral D-0006): 92 of 118 vendored TypeScript files drift from the Prettier config. Reformatting them here was REJECTED as a reformat-the-world commit; instead .prettierignore excludes the pre-existing vendored source, with the reformat scheduled as debt before the next broad backend edit. Draw the distinction carefully when reviewing: an EXPLICIT, documented, ledgered exclusion that says 'we do not format this yet' is a scope statement; silently dropping a KNOWN-FAILING test from a glob (atlasTokens) would hide a failure. The first is acceptable here, the second is not, and the .prettierignore must name the reason and D-0006 rather than sit there bare. New code gets NO such exclusion. ESLint should still cover the vendored source under the conservative syntax-only ruleset; if it genuinely cannot, the vendored source may be excluded from ESLint too — but ONLY recorded in the same deferral, never by weakening the ruleset until it reports nothing. EXCLUSION SHAPE: .prettierignore must list the EXACT pre-existing files (generate with prettier --list-different, ~70), never a directory wildcard — a directory ignore would permanently exempt future backend/contract code and break the 'new code is always format-checked' half of the criterion. The list is self-liquidating and carries a header naming D-0006. TRANSITIVE GUARD: pinning FACTORY_QUALITY_CMD -> `npm run quality` -> `lint && format:check` is NOT enough — the guard must assert the graph recursively down to every runnable leaf (root lint, root format:check, and each workspace's lint/format:check body). Otherwise repointing root `lint` at `echo lint` leaves the declared mapping and the guard green while ESLint never runs. A quality command is only protected when its leaves are. CONFIG COVERAGE, stated honestly: format-check the JSON/YAML/MJS config files this task adds (eslint.config.mjs, .prettierrc.json, the package.json files, quality.yml) and lint the executable MJS. .envrc is SHELL — ESLint and Prettier do not parse it, so do not claim they cover it; the guard test validates it semantically. Reject any wording implying otherwise. DEPENDENCIES (conduct §9): the minimal set is eslint, prettier and typescript-eslint (the TS parser ESLint needs). @eslint/js IS adopted deliberately (human decision 2026-09-07): eslint.config.mjs must build on js.configs.recommended as its base, with typescript-eslint layered for TS parsing — a maintained obvious-error set rather than a hand-rolled rule list. If the config does not actually reference it, that is a finding. CI TRIGGER: `push` only. The current workflow also runs on pull_request, duplicating verification for branch pushes with no stated benefit. TOOLS COVERAGE (resolves S-0010/S-0011): tools/junit-run.mjs and tools/junit-run.test.mjs are in write scope SO THAT THEY CAN BE FORMATTED — 203 lines of factory tooling we own, not vendored product source. Format them and keep the criterion literally true: ALL tools/ MJS is format-checked, with no exclusion and no special case. They do NOT go on the .prettierignore D-0006 list; that list is for pre-existing backend/contract product source only. Formatting them is the whole permitted change — no behaviour edits. HARNESS WORKFLOWS ARE OUT (pre-empting the next block): .github/workflows/factory-scaffold.yml, gardener.yml, harness-health.yml and roadmap-gate.yml all FAIL Prettier today and are HARNESS-OWNED — `forge upgrade` replaces them wholesale (observed this session), so any formatting applied to them is discarded at the next upgrade and they are not ours to edit. The format:check glob must therefore target the config files THIS task adds (.github/workflows/quality.yml, eslint.config.mjs, .prettierrc.json, the package.json files) — NOT a blanket .github/**/*.yml. Add the four harness workflows to .prettierignore under their own header naming this reason, kept separate from the D-0006 product-source list. A blanket YAML glob is a finding. D-0006 MUST NOT BECOME A PERMANENT EXEMPTION (the sharpest remaining risk): Prettier ignores whole FILES, and the ignore list contains files api-surface-trim will edit next — backend/src/config.ts, main.ts, app.module.ts, warehouse/postgres.adapter.ts. Without a rule, NEW lines written into those files silently escape the 'all new code is format-checked' claim. The .prettierignore header must therefore state the binding precondition: BEFORE any task edits a listed file, that task formats the file and REMOVES it from the list in the same change; and any NEW ignore entry requires a named, dated deferral. That is what makes the list self-liquidating rather than a loophole. GUARD LEAVES: pin every runnable leaf the four claims depend on — BOTH workspaces' typecheck bodies (no-emit, not builds), the backend test body (so it cannot become a no-op), the lint/format leaves, and lint eslint.config.mjs itself (it is executable MJS and is currently format-checked but not linted). CI TRIGGER FALSIFIABILITY: finding a `push:` line is not enough — the guard must REJECT additional triggers (pull_request) and push branch filters, so 'every push, push only' is actually falsifiable. LOCAL VERIFY PRECONDITION: verify.py lets a pre-set FACTORY_* value win, so `FACTORY_QUALITY_CMD=true python3 factory/scripts/verify.py` is a false local green. The recorded local evidence must be produced with all four variables UNSET (env -u ...); CI is the enforced authority. DECISION 0011 BOUNDARY: quality.yml is a VERIFICATION workflow — no deploy, no credentials, no environments, no infrastructure. Decision 0011 still defers deployment/CD entirely. Say so, so a later reader does not correctly refuse this workflow as deferred deployment work. TEST RUNNER CORRECTION IS IN SCOPE (verified blocker): the backend suite fails for a SECOND reason beyond atlasTokens — backend/src/branding.identifiers.test.ts resolves "backend/src" and "contract/src" relative to cwd, and the workspace script runs with cwd=backend, so it searches backend/backend/src and fails. FACTORY_TEST_CMD therefore cannot go green without correcting the test INVOCATION. That correction is CONFIGURATION (the npm scripts in the root and backend manifests, both already in write scope) and is explicitly permitted — the hard stop bars remediation of pre-existing SOURCE, not fixing a runner that never worked from the root. Do NOT edit branding.identifiers.test.ts or any other test body to make this pass; correct the invocation so tests run with the repo root as cwd. A clean checkout also lacks contract/dist until the structural build runs, so the aggregate must order build before typecheck/test. GUARD, IMPLEMENTATION-LEVEL: matching a `push:` line is not enforcement — pin the exact `on:` stanza with Node built-ins so adding pull_request or push.branches FAILS. And the .prettierignore headers (the D-0006 self-liquidating rule, and the separate harness-workflow header) must actually EXIST in the file, with a mechanical check that a changed ignored path fails — documentation alone does not protect the claim. Note the debt inventory: D-0006 says 92 files, measured with default Prettier settings before the config existed; under the chosen config it is 71. Record the corrected number. TEST TRANSPILATION (decided here, conduct §9 — justified, not defaulted): the backend suite ALSO fails with TS7006 'implicitly any' errors across pre-existing test files, because ts-node/register TYPE-CHECKS and backend's tsconfig deliberately excludes tests from typecheck scope. Run the tests in TRANSPILE-ONLY mode. Justification: type checking is FACTORY_TYPECHECK_CMD's job and those files are deliberately out of its scope, so making the test runner type-check them duplicates one gate and blocks on pre-existing debt the hard stop forbids remediating. This narrows what the test phase asserts to behaviour, which is what a test phase is for. Do NOT 'fix' the any-types in pre-existing tests and do NOT widen tsconfig — either would be the source remediation the hard stop bars. ORDERING: the aggregate must build contract BEFORE typecheck and test, or every @3f/contract import fails with TS2307 on a clean checkout. SCOPE: plans/deferrals.md is in write scope because this task's contract requires D-0005 and D-0006 ledgered; stage-done measures the diff, so an out-of-scope ledger write would fail the seal. DB-DEPENDENT TESTS (human decision, signal S-0012-f90b, deferral D-0008): 42 backend tests across 8 files need a migrated Postgres app DB, and quality.yml has no database by design. FACTORY_TEST_CMD therefore runs the HERMETIC backend tests plus the guard — the DB-dependent set is demonstrated evidence run on the host against docker-compose, the same treatment signals S-0002..S-0005 received and the same pattern as the spec's WAREHOUSE_E2E=1 gating. Split them by an explicit, readable mechanism (a naming convention or a declared file list), NOT by a silent glob that a future test file could fall through unnoticed: a new DB-backed test must land in the excluded set deliberately, not by accident. Name the split in the .envrc comment and in the guard, so what CI does and does not enforce is legible rather than implied. Do NOT add a Postgres service, migrations, or any infrastructure to the workflow. DURABLE D-0006 ENFORCEMENT (a hole that would ship a fake gate): checking `git diff HEAD` plus untracked files is NOT enough — once a later task COMMITS a change to an ignored file, CI checks out a clean tree, the guard sees no changed path, and that file stays wholly exempt from Prettier forever. The guard must PIN EACH ignored file's baseline content hash: a changed hash FAILS until the path is removed from .prettierignore, at which point the normal glob picks it up. That is what makes the list self-liquidating in fact rather than in prose. ENVRC EFFECTIVE SEMANTICS (second fake-gate hole): verify.py accepts any simple `export` and LAST ASSIGNMENT WINS, while a guard that only reads the first fully-quoted line would stay green if someone appended `export FACTORY_QUALITY_CMD=true` further down — verify.py would then run `true`. The guard must model verify.py's effective-assignment rules and reject any FACTORY_* whose FINAL effective value is not the pinned command, including later, unquoted, or duplicate exports. TEST SPLIT MUST REACH THE SCRIPTS: FACTORY_TEST_CMD currently resolves to the whole backend glob. Introduce explicit `test:hermetic` and `test:db` scripts with declared file lists; CI and FACTORY_TEST_CMD run ONLY test:hermetic. The Verify and Manual Verification sections name the same split — no step may claim 'the whole backend suite green' in CI. CI TRUST BOUNDARY: quality.yml must declare `permissions: contents: read` — without an explicit block it inherits the repository default GITHUB_TOKEN scope, which is broader than the read-only checkout a verification workflow needs, and that quietly contradicts the verification-only claim. Pin every action to an immutable commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment; floating tags are mutable third-party dependencies in a workflow whose whole job is to be trustworthy. REWORK (review round 4, 2026-09-07 — one blocking guard-completeness gap, fix it COMPREHENSIVELY so no intermediate remains): the guard pins `build` and each workspace build body but NOT the root `build:contract`/`build:backend` intermediates that connect them — a no-op repointing there passes the structural gate hollow. Do not just add those two: pin the ENTIRE resolved script graph reachable from every FACTORY_* command AND from verify:ci, recursively to every leaf, so NO intermediate script is unasserted. Concretely: FACTORY_STRUCTURAL_CMD -> structural -> {build -> build:contract, build:backend -> each workspace build body; check_dual_runtime; check_vendor_integrity}; FACTORY_TYPECHECK_CMD -> typecheck -> each workspace typecheck body; FACTORY_QUALITY_CMD -> quality -> lint, format:check (their exact bodies); FACTORY_TEST_CMD -> test:hermetic -> workspace test:hermetic body + the node --test guard; and verify:ci -> structural, typecheck, quality, test:hermetic. Assert every one of those root and workspace script BODIES against a pinned expected value, and add a negative control proving that repointing ANY intermediate (build:contract, build:backend, structural, quality, test:hermetic, a workspace body) at a no-op FAILS the guard. This is the whole remaining gap — resolve the graph once, completely, not one script at a time.

No app screens — the reviewable foundation the shell/login builds on. acceptance_criteria: frontend is a third npm workspace (root workspaces adds "frontend") with a pre-authored tsconfig (Next TS plugin + .next/types include) and a frontend/.gitignore for .next/, next-env.d.ts and *.tsbuildinfo, so `next build` is NON-MUTATING - made falsifiable by the guard (it asserts those .gitignore entries and the tsconfig plugin/include) and by stage-done, which rejects any tracked-file change from verification. The root *:frontend scripts that need the app context (build, dev, typecheck via tsc --noEmit, test via vitest) WRAP the @3f/frontend workspace scripts; build:frontend runs build:contract first (= npm run build:contract && npm -w @3f/frontend run build) as workspace dependency-ordering hygiene and is added to root `build` so `structural`/FACTORY_STRUCTURAL_CMD compiles all three workspaces. @3f/contract is declared as a MANIFEST-level workspace dependency (pinned 0.0.0) - this foundation adds no runtime import (the first genuine consumption is frontend-shell-login's api.ts transport). A minimal root layout (fonts + providers) + a placeholder page exist so the build succeeds; NO Dashboard/shell/nav/top-bar/login screens (frontend-shell-login owns those)

the Tailwind theme is driven entirely by the _ds token variables ported from docs/design/3F-Financial-MIS/_ds/knacklabs-design-system-63be358e-2e64-4441-bcd0-253b9c903a8b/tokens/colors.css, spacing.css and typography.css: the ported token DEFINITION files carry the --kl-* definitions (with the source hex, as a definition must), while the Tailwind config and ALL components CONSUME them via var(--kl-*)/theme tokens with NO raw hex; a hermetic test asserts SET-LEVEL PARITY - every --kl-* variable the source colors/spacing/typography.css defines is present in the ported theme (the D-0005 replacement coverage), with a negative control. fonts.css is NOT ported (its Google @import is design-reference only). The runtime font is a locally vendored Inter VARIABLE WOFF2 from the official immutable rsms/inter release v4.1 (InterVariable.woff2 + OFL.txt); its expected SHA-256 is taken from that official release and committed as the pin in frontend/app/fonts/PROVENANCE.md, and the host seed verifies the downloaded bytes against that PRE-DECLARED expected digest (not a self-computed one). It loads via next/font/local exposing --font-inter; globals set --font-sans: var(--font-inter), <fallbacks> AFTER the token import so the local font is the SINGLE owner. next/font/google is never imported and a hermetic test scans ONLY runtime frontend/ source (app/, src/, config) for next/font/google and fonts.googleapis.com/fonts.gstatic.com. NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 is set in the workspace build script (disabling Next telemetry, not claimed as full network proof); dev:frontend binds loopback 127.0.0.1:3000

a pinned, local, OFFLINE Vitest + React Testing Library + jsdom runner (invoked via `npm exec --no`, never npx) executes from repo root; frontend/vitest.config.ts sets root to the repo root and scopes test.include to frontend/**/*.test.{ts,tsx} so it never discovers the backend suite. tasks.title: Fresh frontend shell + OTP login
tasks.objective: Build the user-facing app shell (Deep Forest left nav + white top bar, branded 3F) and a net-new email+OTP login wired to the backend auth API, faithful to the approved Claude Design, on top of the frontend-foundation scaffold. Server state via TanStack Query over the api.ts transport (credentials:'include' + per-POST 3f_csrf re-read).
acceptance_criteria: the app shell (top bar + left nav) renders in KnackLabs green, branded 3F, faithful to the bound design export docs/design/3F-Financial-MIS/3F Financial MIS.dc.html - Deep Forest (#0C3529) left nav (200px expanded / 62px collapsed, 3F header, user block) + white 56px top bar + Off-White (#F4F7F6) canvas, built ONLY from the _ds --kl-* tokens (no raw hex in components); on mobile (390x844) the left nav collapses to an off-canvas drawer behind a keyboard-focusable toggle that reports aria-expanded, closes on Escape, and returns focus to the toggle. Consumes the frontend-foundation scaffold (theme, next/font/local Inter, TanStack Query provider, shadcn primitives); the D-0012 --text-body/ink token collision is resolved as the theme is applied to real screens (Tailwind ink maps to --kl-ink)

email+OTP login works end-to-end under the spec's local runtime contract: a successful verification lands in the shell, logout returns to /login, and an access-token 401 retries once through POST /api/auth/refresh before falling back to /login. The client (frontend/src/lib/api.ts) uses credentials:'include' against the auth allow-list (GET /api/auth/csrf bootstrap, POST otp/request, POST otp/verify, GET me, POST refresh, POST logout) and sends x-csrf-token re-read from the current 3f_csrf cookie immediately before EVERY mutating request (never cached); server state is TanStack Query (me as a query the route guard reads, otp/logout as mutations that prime/invalidate it)

the login screen implements the spec's normative Login screen contract (docs/specs/app-platform-base.md §Login screen contract): a split screen from _ds tokens (left Deep Forest #0C3529 brand panel with the '3F Financial MIS' wordmark + one value line, Mint #6AF1B0 as a thin on-dark accent only; right a white card on the Off-White canvas; brand panel stacks above the card at 390x844), the two-step flow (email type=email autocomplete=email + Emerald #1C6B49 'Send code' 44px at radius-md; then a 6-digit field inputmode=numeric autocomplete=one-time-code client-validated /^\d{6}$/ with Emerald 'Verify', a 'Use a different email' back link and 'Resend code'), the load-bearing uniform copy ('If that email has access, a code is on its way.' / 'That code didn't match - check it or resend.'), and the accessibility (real <label>s, aria-live=polite acks/errors, focus to the code field after Send and to the first error on failure, :active feedback, ease-out <=200ms entry transitions, prefers-reduced-motion respected), verified by the user-facing functional check at 1440x900 and 390x844

exactly five nav labels (Dashboard, MIS Reports, Ask, Explore / Saved, Admin) render with only Dashboard active (a real route); the other four, the top-bar global search and the data-freshness pill render visibly unavailable (aria-disabled / non-navigable, no dead routes, no 'coming soon' copy, the freshness pill reads as explicitly unavailable) and make NO feature API calls - these are the spec's intentional, enumerated divergences from the active design export, not fidelity failures
